questions.question: What is chromatography highly useful for besides analyzing substances?
options: Separating very large quantities of heavy metals
Separating minute samples of mixtures
Speeding up the chemical reactions of solutes
Creating saturated solutions from insoluble solids

questions.question: If a scientist runs a chromatogram of a completely pure substance, how many spots will be produced?
options: No spots at all
Exactly one spot
Two distinct spots
A continuous streak of many spots

questions.question: What would you expect to see on a chromatogram if the sample tested is a mixture?
options: A single, highly concentrated spot
No spots on the paper
Many different spots
The paper dissolving completely

questions.question: Why is a pencil used to draw the starting line on chromatography paper instead of a pen?
options: Pencil lead is magnetic and stabilizes the paper
Pencil is insoluble in water and will not run with the solvent
Pencil lines react chemically with the chromatography solvent
Pencil is easier to see under ultraviolet light

questions.question: Under what condition is simple distillation typically used to separate a mixture?
options: When the mixture contains only two substances
When there are four or more substances with identical boiling points
When separating insoluble solids from a heavy liquid
When a magnet is needed to extract metallic particles

questions.question: Which separation technique is best suited for separating a mixture containing three or more liquids, or liquids with very close boiling points?
options: Simple distillation
Paper chromatography
Fractional distillation
Decanting using a separating funnel

questions.question: What happens during distillation if the condenser is allowed to warm up?
options: It becomes more effective at collecting the distillate
It becomes less effective and more gas will escape
The boiling point of the liquid in the flask decreases
The solute will begin to crystallize inside the tube

questions.question: Which process describes reforming a solute as crystals from a saturated solution following a change in conditions?
options: Crystallisation
Simple distillation
Decantation
Fractional distillation

questions.question: How can you ensure that larger crystals are formed during the crystallisation process?
options: By boiling the solvent as rapidly as possible
By allowing the solvent to evaporate more slowly
By adding a chemical catalyst to speed up evaporation
By keeping the solution under high pressure

questions.question: Which of the following materials can be separated from a mixture using a magnet?
options: Copper and aluminium
Iron and steel
Zinc and brass
Lead and tin

questions.question: What process is used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid using a filter?
options: Crystallisation
Distillation
Chromatography
Filtration

questions.question: If two immiscible liquids are mixed together and allowed to settle, what will happen?
options: They will dissolve into each other completely
They will react chemically to form a solid precipitate
They do not mix, and one will float above the other
They will turn into a gas at room temperature

questions.question: Which of the following methods can be used to separate two immiscible liquids?
options: Decanting or using a separating funnel
Simple distillation or chromatography
Evaporation followed by filtration
Fractional distillation only

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of miscible liquids when they are left to stand?
options: They will slowly separate into distinct layers
They do not separate into layers
One of the liquids will instantly evaporate
They will form a solid crystal at the bottom

questions.question: Which sequence of techniques is required to separate pure salt from a mixture of rock salt?
options: Chromatography, distillation, and magnetism
Making a solution, filtration, and crystallisation
Fractional distillation, decanting, and evaporation
Magnets, heating, and simple distillation

questions.question: Why should a condenser in a distillation setup be kept cold?
options: To speed up condensation
To prevent the flask from cracking
To lower the boiling point of the mixture
To stop the solute from dissolving
